note: Source of truth for the résumé PDF. frontend/scripts/build-resume.mjs renders it to app/public/resume.pdf on every build; name, role and contact come from content.json so they cannot drift (set role here only to override the headline). Inside summary-level text, **double asterisks** mark a bold run — used for the claim a reader should catch when skimming; a highlight with no asterisks falls back to bolding the thesis up to the first colon. highlights renders as Career Highlights; an experience entry marked "earlier": true moves to the Earlier Experience section. An entry marked "keepTogether": true never splits across pages; one without it may split between bullets, and its title repeats with (continued) at the top of the next page. outside renders as the closing Outside Work line. Page budget: two US Letter pages — any added line must be paid for; the builder prints the page count and warns when it is not two. Voice: a builder's, never an advocate's. Each bullet says what was written, built or run, with what, and what it achieved — verbs of making, real technology, real numbers. No argument scaffolding (no 'preferred X over Y for Z', no 'so/therefore' in every line). Chronology stays true: Eleva was written from 2017 and won Start-Up Chile in 2022; its AI features are from 2026. Length: the summary stays under six lines and every bullet under three; the long version lives on the site's Experience page.
summary: Senior software engineer and cloud architect: 13 years shipping production systems, on AWS since 2014. I wrote Eleva, a multi-tenant SaaS that schools use to evaluate their staff, from the first commit to production — .NET, Angular, PostgreSQL, AWS — and won Start-Up Chile with it in 2022. I still run it. At Electronic Payments I lead the architecture of Liquor Cart, an event-driven commerce platform whose store registers keep selling when the cloud doesn't, and I wrote about 90% of its C#. I like systems that are boring at 3 a.m. and cheap on a Sunday.
highlights: **Designed and wrote a complete SaaS:** Eleva, a multi-tenant evaluation platform for schools — backend, frontend, data model and AWS infrastructure — and took it to production. Won **Start-Up Chile Ignite (2022)**.
**Rebuilt a retailer's commerce platform:** a Magento storefront plus an event-driven .NET middleware on AWS for orders, payments and POS sync. Registers keep selling offline.
**Changed how a company ships:** put Magento under infrastructure as code (CDK) and built the **company's first CI/CD pipelines**, now reused by other projects.

experience.title: Lead Software Architect
bullets: Lead architect of **Liquor Cart**, an omnichannel platform for liquor retailers: Magento 2 storefront, event-driven .NET middleware on AWS, and on-premise registers that **keep selling when the cloud is down**.
Wrote **about 90% of the C#** middleware: domain-driven services on RabbitMQ (MassTransit), retries with a replayable error queue, and one virtual host per store so a failure never leaves that store.
Built the order and catalog store on event sourcing (Marten): **idempotent payment actions**, card data tokenized at the gateway, and an audit trail for every change.
Designed **payment recovery as a saga**: it completes or cancels orders, voids or refunds payments, and hands a person only the cases it cannot resolve.

Put Magento under **infrastructure as code (AWS CDK)** and built the **company's first CI/CD pipelines**: identical environments from a laptop to production, with scheduled shutdowns and routine patching.
Built **40+ Magento admin modules**: a new store with **about 20,000 products goes live in around ten minutes**, and the business inspects or re-syncs the integration without a developer.
Shipped OpenTelemetry tracing, alarms, least-privilege IAM and encrypted secrets from the start. The architecture and pipelines are now **the reference other projects copy**.
Lead a **team of six**: conventions, code review and mentoring, so juniors ship to production safely. 178 merged pull requests, **1,600+ unit tests on every push**.

experience.title: Founder and Platform Architect
bullets: **Designed and wrote the whole product**, and run it in production: a .NET modular monolith, an Angular frontend, PostgreSQL and multi-tenancy, on AWS ECS Fargate.

Schools run 360° staff evaluations on it: a **200-person school's evaluations generate in about five minutes**, results consolidate in **under 20 seconds**, load-tested at **1,000 simultaneous evaluators**.
Every process snapshots its configuration at creation, so past results never change when the rules do. Rubrics are versioned, evidence is attached per question, climate surveys are anonymous at rest.

AWS as code (CDK), CI/CD with automatic rollback: **129 production releases in 30 days** (Oct–Nov 2026). Environments shut down outside school hours; an operations panel shows drift and traces each release to its commit.
2026: opened the platform to companies and health organizations as **Eleva Works, on the same codebase**, with a self-serve trial that creates a working organization at sign-up.

2026: shipped an **AI assistant** for administrators. It reads through the user's own permissions, sees people as pseudonyms, and proposes changes only a person can apply. Scores and reports stay deterministic.
Real-time updates over PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY and long polling: no Redis, no extra infrastructure to run.
